summary: All three hardening layers from Decision 1 are in place: tag allowlist, URL-scheme allowlist with IGNORECASE + ^ anchor (blocks javascript:/data:/file:/vbscript:/relative), CSP meta byte-exact. Attribute-name guard was added during review to close a real injection surface (crafted keys like 'x" onerror="alert(1)' would have broken out of the tag). Unknown tags drop children too (script/style payloads not inlined). No logging of dropped content. Module is side-effect free.

findings.description:
ORIGINALLY: attribute names were emitted verbatim without validation. A crafted attrs key like 'x" onerror="alert(1)' would produce `

`, breaking out of the tag regardless of value escaping.
findings.recommendation: FIXED IN-REVIEW: added _SAFE_ATTR_NAME_RE = ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$ check in _render_attrs. Malformed keys drop the attribute entirely. Test test_malicious_attribute_name_dropped + parametrised test_non_identifier_attribute_name_dropped cover 6 bad-key variants.

findings.description: Inline <style> block is emitted under CSP style-src 'unsafe-inline'. No external URLs, no @font-face, no @import.
findings.recommendation: No action. CSP 'unsafe-inline' is intentional for readability styling; default-src 'none' still blocks everything else.

findings.description: Unknown tags drop both the tag AND its children — correct defensive behaviour; a script payload inside <script>alert</script> is not re-inlined as escaped text.
findings.recommendation: No action. This matches the task spec explicit guidance.
